title: st edit on an unknown id registers it in tracked .intentfiles, and the file argument decides
body:
`intent st edit <UNKNOWN-ID> <file>` registers the unknown id in the TRACKED `intent/.intentfiles` and then fails. The id names a thread that does not exist, the command exits non-zero, and a realisation-policy line for it is now in your working tree waiting to be committed by whoever commits next.

DRIVEN WITH CONTROLS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, against `f4a2271f`. Using ids that exist nowhere:

    st edit ST9997 design        -> WROTE STEELTHREAD:ST9997
    st edit ST9997 impl          -> WROTE
    st edit ST9997 tasks         -> WROTE
    st edit ST9997 acceptance    -> did not write
    st edit ST9996 info          -> did not write
    st edit ST9996               -> did not write  (bare, register default)

THE SPLIT IS THE FINDING AND IT IS NOT THE ONE ALREADY RECORDED. It is not "unrealised clean, manifest-present writes" -- it is the FILE ARGUMENT that decides. The three that write are exactly the AUTHORED files; the three that do not are the two GENERATED VIEWS and the bare default. The generated-view paths refuse before they reach realisation; the authored-file paths realise first and fail afterwards, leaving the registration behind.

So the writing set is precisely the set a user has a legitimate reason to reach for. Nobody types `st edit <id> acceptance` to author something; `design`, `impl` and `tasks` are the whole point of the verb.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, AND THE FIRST ATTRIBUTION WAS WRONG. `STEELTHREAD:ST9999` appeared in the working tree after vc drove `st edit ST9999 info` and `st edit ST9999 design` as controls for a different finding. The first re-test used `info` alone, did not reproduce, and would have closed this as unattributable. It reproduces only when the file argument is one of the three, which is why the per-argument sweep exists and why a single negative control nearly buried it.

IT COMPOUNDS THE UNKNOWN-THREAD DEFECT RATHER THAN SITTING BESIDE IT. `st edit` on an unknown id never reports the id as unknown -- it returns the generated-view refusal or "not a file this artefact carries" depending on the argument. So a typo gets no diagnosis AND silently enters a tracked file. The operator has no signal at either end.

BLAST RADIUS IS A SHARED CHECKOUT. `.intentfiles` is tracked and has many writers by design, so a line planted by one node's typo is picked up by whichever node commits that path next, under their authorship, in a commit about something else. On this estate four sessions share one worktree.

Existing record: `intent/restart.md` already carries "`intent edit` AND `intent st edit` WRITE ON THEIR rc=1 REFUSAL PATH" with a state-based precondition. That entry is correct and its precondition is incomplete -- this is the argument-based axis, and it was measured after the state-based one had been swept twice by two nodes who both published clean.

Driven by vc, 2026-08-29, on the estate's own tree; both planted lines removed after measurement.
